findings.title: Accessible name concatenates chat name with 'Pinned'
findings.problem: The sr-only span is appended directly after the chat-name text inside the same button with no whitespace text node between them (JSX strips the newline), so accessible-name computation in Chromium yields e.g. 'Test ChatPinned' or '…Pinned'. Flagged independently by both the blind and edge-case lenses.
findings.impact: Screen readers may announce the name and pinned state as one run-together word, degrading the exact announcement this WCAG 1.1.1 fix exists to provide; the /pinned/i regex test cannot catch it.
findings.recommendation: Add a separator inside the span, e.g. , pinned or a leading space (' Pinned'), so the accessible name tokenizes as 'Test Chat, pinned'.

findings.title: No negative test for the unpinned path
findings.problem: The new behavior is only asserted positively; nothing asserts that an unpinned chat's button accessible name does NOT match /pinned/i. Flagged independently by both the blind and edge-case lenses.
findings.impact: A regression that renders the sr-only span unconditionally (or moves it) would mislabel every chat as pinned to AT users while the suite stays green.
findings.recommendation: Add a companion test rendering {...mockChat, pinned: false} and asserting screen.queryByRole('button', { name: /pinned/i }) is not in the document.
